items.stem: How is price elasticity of supply calculated?
options: Percentage change in quantity supplied ÷ percentage change in price
Percentage change in price ÷ percentage change in quantity supplied
Change in quantity supplied ÷ change in price
Percentage change in quantity demanded ÷ percentage change in price
items.answer: Percentage change in quantity supplied ÷ percentage change in price
items.markingKey: PES = %ΔQs/%ΔP; usually positive.

items.stem: Explain what a PES value of 2.5 means.
items.answer: A 1% rise in price leads to a 2.5% rise in quantity supplied: supply is price elastic, so producers can respond strongly.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: interpretation; 1 mark: elastic [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between perfectly elastic and perfectly inelastic supply.
items.answer: Perfectly inelastic (PES = 0): quantity fixed whatever the price (vertical curve). Perfectly elastic (PES = ∞): any quantity supplied at one price (horizontal curve).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: When the price of car tyres rose from $10 to $14, the quantity supplied rose from 200 to 360 units a month. Calculate the price elasticity of supply.

When the price of car tyres rose from $20 to $21, the quantity supplied rose from 1,000 to 1040 units a month. (a) Calculate the PES and state whether supply is elastic or inelastic. (b) Suggest two reasons why supply of car tyres might have this elasticity.
items.answer: (a) PES = 0.8: price inelastic. (b) Long production time, no spare capacity, few stocks, immobile factors.
items.markingKey: (a) 4/5 = 0.8 [2]; interpretation [1] (b) two consistent reasons [2] [5]

items.stem: Extract: Average monthly rents for flats in Karachi rose from $150 to $210 over two years, while the number of flats available rose from 10,000 to 10,400. Builders say planning rules and a shortage of skilled construction workers make it hard to build more quickly. In contrast, the supply of rental scooters in the city doubled within months when prices rose. (a) Calculate the price elasticity of supply of flats. (b) Explain why the supply of rental scooters is more elastic than the supply of flats.
items.answer: (a) 0.1 (b) Scooters can be bought and delivered quickly; low capital cost; easy entry.
items.markingKey: (a) 4% ÷ 40% [2] (b) Credit: Scooters can be bought and delivered quickly; low capital cost; easy entry. [2]

items.stem: A PES of 0.3 means supply is
items.answer: price inelastic
items.markingKey: PES < 1.

items.stem: Northwind can quickly increase production of chocolate bars from its large stocks when the price rises. Explain the likely PES.
items.answer: Elastic supply (PES > 1): stocks allow quantity supplied to rise more than proportionately to price.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: elastic; 1 mark: stocks [2]

items.stem: Silverline can quickly increase production of car tyres from its large stocks when the price rises. Explain the likely PES.
items.answer: Elastic supply (PES > 1): stocks allow quantity supplied to rise more than proportionately to price.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: elastic; 1 mark: stocks [2]

items.stem: The price of tickets for a football final in Mumbai doubles but the number of seats stays the same. Explain what this shows about PES.
items.answer: Supply is perfectly inelastic (PES = 0): the stadium has a fixed capacity.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: PES = 0; 1 mark: fixed capacity [2]

items.answer: (a) PES = 0.5: price inelastic. (b) Long production time, no spare capacity, few stocks, immobile factors.
items.markingKey: (a) 12.5/25 = 0.5 [2]; interpretation [1] (b) two consistent reasons [2] [5]

items.stem: Which would make supply of a good more price elastic?
options: Firms have large stocks of finished goods
Firms are working at full capacity
items.answer: Firms have large stocks of finished goods
items.markingKey: Stocks, spare capacity, factor mobility, time, short production period.

items.stem: Explain two factors that determine the price elasticity of supply of a product.
items.answer: Spare capacity; stocks; factor mobility; time period; length of production process; ease of entry.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each factor, 1 mark each explained [4]

items.stem: Explain why the supply of housing in a city is likely to be price inelastic.
items.answer: Building takes a long time, land is limited and planning permission is needed, so the number of homes cannot rise quickly when prices rise.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: time/land; 1 mark: planning/limited response [2]

items.stem: A bakery in Cairo can easily switch its ovens from bread to cakes. What is the likely price elasticity of supply?
items.answer: Elastic supply
items.markingKey: Elastic supply: factors are mobile between uses.

items.stem: Only a few highly trained surgeons can perform a new operation in Dravonia. What is the likely price elasticity of supply? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Inelastic supply: specialist skills make labour immobile in the short run.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Inelastic supply; 1 mark: explanation – specialist skills make labour immobile in the short run. [2]

items.stem: Explain why manufactured goods often have more elastic supply than primary products.
items.answer: Factories can use spare capacity, overtime and stocks quickly; crops and minerals depend on growing seasons and long development times.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: manufactured flexibility; 1 mark: primary constraints [2]

items.stem: The price of steel pipes in Loristan rises sharply but firms are already operating at full capacity. Explain the likely effect on output in the short run.
items.answer: Supply is inelastic: without spare capacity or stocks, output can rise only slightly, so most of the effect is on price.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: inelastic; 1 mark: little output response [2]

items.answer: Perfectly inelastic supply

items.stem: After a 20% rise in the price of electric scooters, the quantity supplied rose by 5% within three months and by 30% after three years. (a) Calculate the short-run and long-run PES. (b) Explain why the two values differ.
items.answer: (a) SR 0.25, LR 1.5. (b) In the short run capacity and other factors are fixed; over time firms invest in new capacity, new firms enter and factors move, so supply becomes more elastic.

items.stem: If supply is price inelastic, an increase in demand will mainly cause
options: a large rise in quantity and a small rise in price
a large rise in price and a small rise in quantity
items.answer: a large rise in price and a small rise in quantity
items.markingKey: Inelastic supply: price absorbs most of the change.

items.stem: Why do prices of agricultural products tend to be volatile?
options: Supply is inelastic in the short run and affected by weather
items.answer: Supply is inelastic in the short run and affected by weather
items.markingKey: Inelastic supply + supply shocks + inelastic demand.

items.stem: Explain why the elasticity of supply affects how much the price changes when demand rises.
items.answer: If supply is elastic, output expands easily so most of the adjustment is in quantity and price rises little; if inelastic, output cannot expand, so price rises a lot.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: elastic case; 1 mark: inelastic case [2]

Price rises by about 53.3% and quantity by about 6.7%
Price rises by about 26.7% and quantity by about 13.3%

items.stem: Demand for fresh fish increases so that, at the original price, buyers want 40% more. The PES is 0.5 and the PED is −0.5. items.stem: Newspapers in Rovania have recently reported a lively debate among economists on this issue. (a) Explain the factors that determine the price elasticity of supply. (b) Assess the extent to which time is the most important determinant of the price elasticity of supply.

items.stem: Extract: Average monthly rents for flats in Dhaka rose from $150 to $210 over two years, while the number of flats available rose from 12,000 to 12,600. Builders say planning rules and a shortage of skilled construction workers make it hard to build more quickly. In contrast, the supply of rental scooters in the city doubled within months when prices rose. (a) Calculate the price elasticity of supply of flats. (b) Explain why the supply of rental scooters is more elastic than the supply of flats.
items.answer: (a) 0.12 (b) Scooters can be bought and delivered quickly; low capital cost; easy entry.
